sanskrit: nala uvāca na me 'parādhaṃ kṛtavāṃs tvaṃ svalpam api pārthiva kṛte 'pi ca na me kopaḥ kṣantavyaṃ hi mayā tava
english: Nala said: You have not committed even the slightest offence against me, O king; and even if you had, I would not be angry — for I must forgive you.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ hy asi sakhā me 'si saṃbandhī ca narādhipa ata ūrdhvaṃ tu bhūyas tvaṃ prītim āhartum arhasi
english: For you are my old friend and my kinsman, O lord of men; and from this day forward you should show me even greater affection.

sanskrit: sarvakāmaiḥ suvihitaḥ sukham asmy uṣitas tvayi na tathā svagṛhe rājan yathā tava gṛhe sadā
english: I have dwelt happily in your house, provided with every comfort; indeed, O king, I was never so well cared for even in my own home.

sanskrit: idaṃ caiva hayajñānaṃ tvadīyaṃ mayi tiṣṭhati tad upākartum icchāmi manyase yadi pārthiva
english: This science of horses that belongs to you still remains with me; I wish to render it back to you now, if you so agree, O king.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca evam uktvā dadau vidyām ṛtuparṇāya naiṣadhaḥ sa ca tāṃ pratijagrāha vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Having spoken thus, the king of Niṣadha imparted the science to Ṛtuparṇa, and he received it in accordance with the rite prescribed.

sanskrit: tato gṛhyāśvahṛdayaṃ tadā bhāṅgasvarir nṛpaḥ sūtam anyam upādāya yayau svapuram eva hi
english: Then, having obtained the secret lore of horses, the king Bhāṅgasvari took another charioteer and departed for his own city.

sanskrit: ṛtuparṇe pratigate nalo rājā viśāṃ pate nagare kuṇḍine kālaṃ nātidīrgham ivāvasat
english: After Ṛtuparṇa had departed, King Nala, O lord of the people, remained in the city of Kuṇḍina for not too long a time.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca sa māsam uṣya kaunteya bhīmam āmantrya naiṣadhaḥ purād alpaparīvāro jagāma niṣadhān prati
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Having stayed a month, O son of Kuntī, the king of Niṣadha took leave of Bhīma and set out toward Niṣadha with a small retinue.

sanskrit: rathenaikena śubhreṇa dantibhiḥ pariṣoḍaśaiḥ pañcāśadbhir hayaiś caiva ṣaṭśataiś ca padātibhiḥ
english: He went with a single splendid chariot, sixteen elephants, fifty horses, and six hundred foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: sa kampayann iva mahīṃ tvaramāṇo mahīpatiḥ praviveśātisaṃrabdhas tarasaiva mahāmanāḥ
english: That great-minded lord of the earth, trembling with eagerness, as if shaking the very ground, entered swiftly and with intense resolve.

sanskrit: tataḥ puṣkaram āsādya vīrasenasuto nalaḥ uvāca dīvyāva punar bahu vittaṃ mayārjitam
english: Then Nala, son of Vīrasena, confronted Puṣkara and said: Let us play again — I have earned great wealth.

sanskrit: damayantī ca yac cānyan mayā vasu samarjitam eṣa vai mama saṃnyāsas tava rājyaṃ tu puṣkara
english: Damayantī and whatever other wealth I have acquired — this is my stake. Your kingdom, O Puṣkara, is the wager on your side.

sanskrit: punaḥ pravartatāṃ dyūtam iti me niścitā matiḥ ekapāṇena bhadraṃ te prāṇayoś ca paṇāvahe
english: Let the dice game resume — such is my firm resolve. With a single throw, and let it be well for you; we shall wager even our lives.

sanskrit: jitvā parasvam āhṛtya rājyaṃ vā yadi vā vasu pratipāṇaḥ pradātavyaḥ paraṃ hi dhanam ucyate
english: Having won and seized another's wealth — whether a kingdom or goods — the counter-stake must be given; for the property of another is said to be the highest wealth at stake.

sanskrit: na ced vāñchasi tad dyūtaṃ yuddhadyūtaṃ pravartatām dvairathenāstu vai śāntis tava vā mama vā nṛpa
english: If you do not wish to play at dice, then let the dice of battle commence; let there be a duel by chariot, and whichever of us wins, O king — let that be the end of it.

sanskrit: vaṃśabhojyam idaṃ rājyaṃ mārgitavyaṃ yathā tathā yena tenāpy upāyena vṛddhānām iti śāsanam
english: This kingdom that is the heritage of our lineage must be recovered by whatever means — that is the teaching of the elders.

sanskrit: dvayor ekatare buddhiḥ kriyatām adya puṣkara kaitavenākṣavatyāṃ vā yuddhe vā namyatāṃ dhanuḥ
english: Let one of the two decisions be made today, O Puṣkara — either bend the bow in the game of dice or bend it in battle.

sanskrit: naiṣadhenaivam uktas tu puṣkaraḥ prahasann iva dhruvam ātmajayaṃ matvā pratyāha pṛthivīpatim
english: Thus addressed by the king of Niṣadha, Puṣkara laughed as if certain of his own victory, and replied to the lord of the earth.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tvayārjitaṃ vittaṃ pratipāṇāya naiṣadha diṣṭyā ca duṣkṛtaṃ karma damayantyāḥ kṣayaṃ gatam diṣṭyā ca dhriyase rājan sadāro 'rinibarhaṇa
english: By good fortune you have earned wealth to serve as the counter-stake, O king of Niṣadha; by good fortune the evil done to Damayantī has come to an end; and by good fortune you still live, O king, together with your wife, O crusher of foes.

sanskrit: dhanena anena vaidarbhī jitena samalaṃkṛtā mām upasthāsyati vyaktaṃ divi śakram ivāpsarāḥ
english: With this wealth, once won, the princess of Vidarbha, adorned in full, will surely attend upon me as an apsarā attends upon Indra in heaven.

sanskrit: nityaśo hi smarāmi tvāṃ pratīkṣāmi ca naiṣadha devane ca mama prītir na bhavaty asuhṛdgaṇaiḥ
english: For I have always remembered you and awaited you, O king of Niṣadha; and I take no pleasure in gambling with those who are not my friends.

sanskrit: jitvā tv adya varārohāṃ damayantīm aninditām kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyāmi sā hi me nityaśo hṛdi
english: But having won today the blameless Damayantī of noble form, I shall consider my purpose fulfilled — for she is ever in my heart.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu tasya tā vāco bahvabaddhapralāpinaḥ iyeṣa sa śiraś chettuṃ khaḍgena kupito nalaḥ
english: Hearing those many incoherent and boastful words of his, Nala, filled with fury, desired to cut off his head with his sword.

sanskrit: smayaṃs tu roṣatāmrākṣas tam uvāca tato nṛpaḥ paṇāvaḥ kiṃ vyāharase jitvā vai vyāhariṣyasi
english: But smiling, his eyes red with anger, the king then said to him: Why do you boast before the wager? Speak after you have won.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāvartata dyūtaṃ puṣkarasya nalasya ca ekapāṇena bhadraṃ te nalena sa parājitaḥ saratnakośanicayaḥ prāṇena paṇito 'pi ca
english: Then the game of dice began between Puṣkara and Nala; with a single throw — and let it be well for you — Puṣkara was defeated by Nala, along with all his treasury of gems, even though his very life had been wagered.

sanskrit: jitvā ca puṣkaraṃ rājā prahasann idam abravīt mama sarvam idaṃ rājyam avyagraṃ hatakaṇṭakam
english: Having won, the king laughed and declared: This entire kingdom is mine, undisturbed and free of thorns.

sanskrit: vaidarbhī na tvayā śakyā rājāpasada vīkṣitum tasyās tvaṃ saparīvāro mūḍha dāsatvam āgataḥ
english: The princess of Vidarbha cannot even be looked upon by you, O vile king; you and your retinue, O fool, have now come to servitude before her.

sanskrit: na tat tvayā kṛtaṃ karma yenāhaṃ nirjitaḥ purā kalinā tat kṛtaṃ karma tvaṃ tu mūḍha na budhyase nāhaṃ parakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ tvayy ādhāsye kathaṃ cana
english: It was not by your deed that I was defeated before — that deed was done by Kali, though you, O fool, do not understand this. I will not lay upon you the fault that was done by another.

sanskrit: yathāsukhaṃ tvaṃ jīvasva prāṇān abhyutsṛjāmi te tathaiva ca mama prītis tvayi vīra na saṃśayaḥ
english: Live in happiness — I release your life; and my affection for you, O hero, remains undimmed, of that there is no doubt.

sanskrit: saubhrātraṃ caiva me tvatto na kadā cit prahāsyati puṣkara tvaṃ hi me bhrātā saṃjīvasva śataṃ samāḥ
english: My brotherly love toward you will never perish, O Puṣkara; for you are truly my brother. Live a hundred years.

sanskrit: evaṃ nalaḥ sāntvayitvā bhrātaraṃ satyavikramaḥ svapuraṃ preṣayām āsa pariṣvajya punaḥ punaḥ
english: Having thus comforted his brother, the valiant Nala embraced him again and again and sent him off to his own city.

sanskrit: sāntvito naiṣadhenaivaṃ puṣkaraḥ pratyuvāca tam puṇyaślokaṃ tadā rājann abhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Thus consoled by the king of Niṣadha, Puṣkara saluted that king of holy renown with joined palms and replied.

sanskrit: kīrtir astu tavākṣayyā jīva varṣāyutaṃ sukhī yo me vitarasi prāṇān adhiṣṭhānaṃ ca pārthiva
english: May your fame be imperishable; live happily for ten thousand years — you who grant me both my life and my dwelling, O king.

sanskrit: sa tathā satkṛto rājñā māsam uṣya tadā nṛpaḥ prayayau svapuraṃ hṛṣṭaḥ puṣkaraḥ svajanāvṛtaḥ
english: Thus honoured by the king, Puṣkara stayed a month, then departed joyfully for his own city, surrounded by his kinsmen.

sanskrit: mahatyā senayā rājan vinītaiḥ paricārakaiḥ bhrājamāna ivādityo vapuṣā puruṣarṣabha
english: With a great army, O king, and with well-disciplined attendants, he departed blazing in his person like the sun, O bull among men.

sanskrit: prasthāpya puṣkaraṃ rājā vittavantam anāmayam praviveśa puraṃ śrīmān atyartham upaśobhitam praviśya sāntvayām āsa paurāṃś ca niṣadhādhipaḥ
english: Having sent off Puṣkara, now wealthy and in good health, the glorious king entered his greatly adorned city; and having entered, the lord of Niṣadha comforted his townspeople.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca praśānte tu pure hṛṣṭe saṃpravṛtte mahotsave mahatyā senayā rājā damayantīm upānayat
english: Bṛhadaśva said: When the city had become peaceful and joyful, and a great festival was under way, the king, with a great army, brought Damayantī home.

sanskrit: damayantīm api pitā satkṛtya paravīrahā prasthāpayad ameyātmā bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ
english: And Damayantī's father, the immeasurable-spirited Bhīma of formidable valour, who destroys the heroes of his enemies, honoured her and sent her forth.

sanskrit: āgatāyāṃ tu vaidarbhyāṃ saputrāyāṃ nalo nṛpaḥ vartayām āsa mudito devarāḍ iva nandane
english: When the princess of Vidarbha arrived with her children, King Nala dwelt in joy like the king of the gods in Nandana.

sanskrit: tathā prakāśatāṃ yāto jambūdvīpe 'tha rājasu punaḥ sve cāvasad rājye pratyāhṛtya mahāyaśāḥ
english: And thus having risen to eminence among the kings of Jambūdvīpa, the great-famed Nala dwelt again in his own kingdom, having recovered it.

sanskrit: īje ca vividhair yajñair vidhivat svāptadakṣiṇaiḥ tathā tvam api rājendra sasuhṛd vakṣyase 'cirāt
english: He performed various sacrifices with proper rites and with generous fees. In the same way, you too, O king of kings, will soon be spoken of together with your friends.

sanskrit: duḥkham etādṛśaṃ prāpto nalaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ devanena naraśreṣṭha sabhāryo bharatarṣabha
english: Such great sorrow was suffered by Nala, conqueror of enemy cities — through gambling, O best of men, O bull of the Bharata line — together with his wife.

sanskrit: ekākinaiva sumahan nalena pṛthivīpate duḥkham āsāditaṃ ghoraṃ prāptaś cābhyudayaḥ punaḥ
english: Entirely alone, O lord of the earth, Nala endured enormous and terrible suffering, and yet he attained prosperity once more.

sanskrit: tvaṃ punar bhrātṛsahitaḥ kṛṣṇayā caiva pāṇḍava ramase 'smin mahāraṇye dharmam evānucintayan
english: But you, O Pāṇḍava, are together with your brothers and with Kṛṣṇā, dwelling happily in this great forest, meditating only on righteousness.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaiś ca mahābhāgair vedavedāṅgapāragair nityam anvāsyase rājaṃs tatra kā paridevanā
english: You are constantly attended by greatly blessed brahmins who are versed in the Vedas and their ancillaries, O king — what cause for lamentation is there?

sanskrit: itihāsam imaṃ cāpi kalināśanam ucyate śakyam āśvāsituṃ śrutvā tvadvidhena viśāṃ pate
english: And this story is said to destroy the power of Kali; a man of your sort, O lord of the people, is able to find consolation upon hearing it.

sanskrit: asthiratvaṃ ca saṃcintya puruṣārthasya nityadā tasyāye ca vyaye caiva samāśvasihi mā śucaḥ
english: Reflecting always on the impermanence of human fortune — its rise and its fall — be consoled and do not grieve.

sanskrit: ye cedaṃ kathayiṣyanti nalasya caritaṃ mahat śroṣyanti cāpy abhīkṣṇaṃ vai nālakṣmīs tān bhajiṣyati arthās tasyopapatsyante dhanyatāṃ ca gamiṣyati
english: Those who will recount this great story of Nala, and those who will hear it repeatedly — ill-fortune will not befall them; wealth will come to them and they will attain blessedness.

sanskrit: itihāsam imaṃ śrutvā purāṇaṃ śaśvad uttamam putrān pautrān paśūṃś caiva vetsyate nṛṣu cāgryatām arogaḥ prītimāṃś caiva bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: Having heard this ancient and ever-excellent story, one will obtain sons, grandsons, and cattle, and will attain pre-eminence among men; he will be free from disease and full of joy — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: bhayaṃ paśyasi yac ca tvam āhvayiṣyati māṃ punaḥ akṣajña iti tat te 'haṃ nāśayiṣyāmi pārthiva
english: The fear you have that someone may challenge you again, calling you ignorant of dice — that fear I will destroy for you, O king.

sanskrit: vedākṣahṛdayaṃ kṛtsnam ahaṃ satyaparākrama upapadyasva kaunteya prasanno 'haṃ bravīmi te
english: I know the complete secret lore of the Vedas and of dice, O you of true valour; receive it, O son of Kuntī — I speak to you with goodwill.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato hṛṣṭamanā rājā bṛhadaśvam uvāca ha bhagavann akṣahṛdayaṃ jñātum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king, with a joyful heart, said to Bṛhadaśva: Venerable sir, I wish to know the secret of dice in its true nature.

sanskrit: tato 'kṣahṛdayaṃ prādāt pāṇḍavāya mahātmane dattvā cāśvaśiro 'gacchad upaspraṣṭuṃ mahātapāḥ
english: Then he imparted the secret lore of dice to the great-souled Pāṇḍava; and having given it, the great ascetic went to the horse-shrine to perform his ablutions.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśve gate pārtham aśrauṣīt savyasācinam vartamānaṃ tapasy ugre vāyubhakṣaṃ manīṣiṇam
english: After Bṛhadaśva had departed, Pārtha heard that the wise Savyasācin was engaged in fierce austerities, living on air alone.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇebhyas tapasvibhyaḥ saṃpatadbhyas tatas tataḥ tīrthaśailavarebhyaś ca sametebhyo dṛḍhavrataḥ
english: He heard this from ascetic brahmins arriving from various places, and from those who had gathered from the best of sacred fords and mountains — he who was firm in his vows.

sanskrit: iti pārtho mahābāhur durāpaṃ tapa āsthitaḥ na tathā dṛṣṭapūrvo 'nyaḥ kaś cid ugratapā iti
english: So Pārtha of the mighty arms had undertaken an austerity hard to attain — "such a fierce ascetic as this has never been seen before" — thus it was said.

sanskrit: yathā dhanaṃjayaḥ pārthas tapasvī niyatavrataḥ munir ekacaraḥ śrīmān dharmo vigrahavān iva
english: Dhanaṃjaya Pārtha was thus an ascetic, firm in his vows, a sage moving alone, glorious, like Dharma himself embodied.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā pāṇḍavo rājaṃs tapyamānaṃ mahāvane anvaśocata kaunteyaḥ priyaṃ vai bhrātaraṃ jayam
english: Hearing of him thus engaged in austerity in the great forest, O king, the son of Kuntī lamented for his beloved brother Jaya.

sanskrit: dahyamānena tu hṛdā śaraṇārthī mahāvane brāhmaṇān vividhajñānān paryapṛcchad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: With his heart burning, Yudhiṣṭhira, seeking refuge, questioned the brahmins of various kinds of knowledge in the great forest.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca bhagavan kāmyakāt pārthe gate me prapitāmahe pāṇḍavāḥ kim akurvanta tam ṛte savyasācinam
english: Janamejaya said: Blessed one, when Pārtha, my great-grandfather, had gone from Kāmyaka, what did the Pāṇḍavas do without that left-handed archer?

sanskrit: sa hi teṣāṃ maheṣvāso gatir āsīd anīkajit ādityānāṃ yathā viṣṇus tathaiva pratibhāti me
english: For he was their great bowman, their refuge, the conqueror of armies — he appears to me as Viṣṇu is among the Ādityas.

sanskrit: tenendrasamavīryeṇa saṃgrāmeṣv anivartinā vinābhūtā vane vīrāḥ katham āsan pitāmahāḥ
english: Separated from him who was equal in valour to Indra and who never turned back in battle, how did those heroic forefathers of mine fare in the forest?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca gate tu kāmyakāt tāta pāṇḍave savyasācini babhūvuḥ kauraveyās te duḥkhaśokaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the Pāṇḍava Savyasācin had departed from Kāmyaka, O dear one, those descendants of Kuru became wholly absorbed in grief and sorrow.

sanskrit: ākṣiptasūtrā maṇayaś chinnapakṣā iva dvijāḥ aprītamanasaḥ sarve babhūvur atha pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Like gems with their strings snapped, like birds with their wings cut, all the Pāṇḍavas became joyless in heart.

sanskrit: vanaṃ ca tad abhūt tena hīnam akliṣṭakarmaṇā kubereṇa yathā hīnaṃ vanaṃ caitrarathaṃ tathā
english: And that forest, deprived of him whose deeds were without blemish, became like the forest of Caitraratha bereft of Kubera.

sanskrit: tam ṛte puruṣavyāghraṃ pāṇḍavā janamejaya mudam aprāpnuvanto vai kāmyake nyavasaṃs tadā
english: Without that tiger among men, O Janamejaya, the Pāṇḍavas dwelt in Kāmyaka unable to find any delight.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇārthe parākrāntāḥ śuddhair bāṇair mahārathāḥ nighnanto bharataśreṣṭha medhyān bahuvidhān mṛgān
english: Striving for the sake of the brahmins, those great warriors slew many kinds of sacrificially pure deer with clean arrows, O best of the Bharata line.

sanskrit: nityaṃ hi puruṣavyāghrā vanyāhāram ariṃdamāḥ viprasṛtya samāhṛtya brāhmaṇebhyo nyavedayan
english: For those tigers among men, those tamers of foes, ever going forth and gathering forest food, they regularly offered it to the brahmins.

sanskrit: evaṃ te nyavasaṃs tatra sotkaṇṭhāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ ahṛṣṭamanasaḥ sarve gate rājan dhanaṃjaye
english: Thus those bulls among men dwelt there full of yearning, all joyless in heart, O king, now that Dhanaṃjaya had gone.

sanskrit: atha viproṣitaṃ vīraṃ pāñcālī madhyamaṃ patim smarantī pāṇḍavaśreṣṭham idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then Pāñcālī, remembering the hero, the middle husband, the best of the Pāṇḍavas who was away, spoke these words.

sanskrit: yo 'rjunenārjunas tulyo dvibāhur bahubāhunā tam ṛte pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhaṃ vanaṃ na pratibhāti me śūnyām iva ca paśyāmi tatra tatra mahīm imām
english: He who, though two-armed Arjuna, is Arjuna's equal with his many arms — without that best of Pāṇḍavas, the forest does not appear beautiful to me; everywhere I look I see this earth as if empty.

sanskrit: bahvāścaryam idaṃ cāpi vanaṃ kusumitadrumam na tathā ramaṇīyaṃ me tam ṛte savyasācinam
english: This wonderful forest with its flowering trees — without the left-handed archer it is not as charming to me.

sanskrit: nīlāmbudasamaprakhyaṃ mattamātaṅgavikramam tam ṛte puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ kāmyakaṃ nātibhāti me
english: Without him — dark as a rain cloud, with the gait of a lordly elephant, with lotus eyes — Kāmyaka does not shine bright for me.

sanskrit: yasya sma dhanuṣo ghoṣaḥ śrūyate 'śaninisvanaḥ na labhe śarma taṃ rājan smarantī savyasācinam
english: He whose bow resounds like the crash of a thunderbolt — remembering the left-handed archer, O king, I find no peace.

sanskrit: tathā lālapyamānāṃ tāṃ niśamya paravīrahā bhīmaseno mahārāja draupadīm idam abravīt
english: Hearing her lamenting thus, Bhīmasena, the slayer of enemy heroes, O great king, spoke these words to Draupadī.

sanskrit: manaḥprītikaraṃ bhadre yad bravīṣi sumadhyame tan me prīṇāti hṛdayam amṛtaprāśanopamam
english: What you say, O gracious slender-waisted one, brings joy to the mind; it gladdens my heart like the drinking of nectar.

sanskrit: yasya dīrghau samau pīnau bhujau parighasaṃnibhau maurvīkṛtakiṇau vṛttau khaḍgāyudhagadādharau
english: He whose two arms are long, even, full, like iron bars, hardened with the calluses of the bowstring, rounded, bearing sword and weapon and mace —

sanskrit: niṣkāṅgadakṛtāpīḍau pañcaśīrṣāv ivoragau tam ṛte puruṣavyāghraṃ naṣṭasūryam idaṃ vanam
english: Adorned with golden armlets and diadems, like two five-headed serpents — without that tiger among men, this forest is as if its sun has vanished.

sanskrit: yam āśritya mahābāhuṃ pāñcālāḥ kuravas tathā surāṇām api yattānāṃ pṛtanāsu na bibhyati
english: Relying upon him of the mighty arms, the Pāñcālas and the Kurus alike do not fear even the arrayed armies of the gods.

sanskrit: yasya bāhū samāśritya vayaṃ sarve mahātmanaḥ manyāmahe jitān ājau parān prāptāṃ ca medinīm
english: Relying upon the arms of that great-souled one, we all consider our enemies defeated in battle and the earth already won.
